title: ABLE or IBLE?
kidRule: There is no perfect rule, but here is a great tip: if you take the ending off and a whole word is left, like WASH in WASHABLE, it is usually A-B-L-E. If what is left is not a word, like POSS in POSSIBLE, it is usually I-B-L-E.
hint: Listen to the 'uh-bul' ending. Now cover that ending up in your mind: is a whole word left over, or not? That is your clue for how the ending starts.
reminder: The 'uh-bul' ending has two spellings: A-B-L-E and I-B-L-E. If your first try did not work, try the other one!

check.question: Why does WASHABLE end with A-B-L-E?
check.correctAnswer: Because when you take the ending off, a whole word (WASH) is left, and that usually means A-B-L-E!
distractors: Because A-B-L-E is always used for words about water
Because a word with S-H in it can never end with I-B-L-E

words.def: Able to be cleaned with water without being ruined.
words.sent: Luckily, the paint on my shirt was washable.
words.story: Some money is washable! Countries like Australia and Canada print their bills on thin plastic, so they can survive a trip through the washing machine.
words.card: My elephant is *washable*, but it takes ten hoses to *wash* him!

words.def: Able to happen or be done.
words.sent: Is it possible to touch your nose with your tongue?
words.story: It is possible to see a rainbow at night! It is called a moonbow, and it is made by moonlight instead of sunlight.
words.card: The *poss*um said anything is *possible*, then rode off on a skateboard!

words.def: Feeling cozy and relaxed, or making you feel that way.
words.sent: This squishy chair is so comfortable.
words.story: Sea otters stay comfortable in icy water because they have the thickest fur of any animal, with up to a million hairs on each square inch!
words.card: My pillow *fort* is so *comfortable* that the dog moved in!

words.def: Easy to crack or smash into pieces.
words.sent: Be careful with that vase because it is breakable.
words.story: Glass is breakable, but it can be melted down and recycled again and again without ever wearing out!
words.card: Take a *break* before you juggle those *breakable* eggs!

words.sent: The spilled milk made a terrible smell in the car.
words.card: The dinosaur made a *terrible* mess eating barbecue *rib*s!

words.sent: Air is invisible, but you can feel it when the wind blows.
words.story: Glass frogs have see-through skin on their tummies, and when they sleep on a leaf they are almost invisible!
words.card: My *invisible* friend came to *visi*t, but I couldn't find him anywhere!

words.sent: That medicine had a horrible taste.
words.story: The durian fruit smells so horrible to some people that it is not allowed on the trains in Singapore!
words.card: The *hor*se sang a *horrible* song and all the cows ran away!

words.def: So amazing that it is hard to believe.
words.sent: The acrobat did an incredible flip in the air.
words.story: A flea can make an incredible jump: more than 100 times the length of its own body!
words.card: The *incredible* parrot painted itself *red* and pretended to be a fire truck!

words.sent: We had an enjoyable afternoon at the beach.
words.story: Rats find tickling enjoyable! When scientists tickle them, they make tiny happy squeaks that are too high for people to hear.
words.card: Jumping for *joy* on a jelly trampoline is very *enjoyable*!

words.def: Small or light enough to carry around easily.
words.sent: We took a portable speaker to the picnic.
words.story: The first portable phone, made in 1973, weighed more than two pounds, about as much as a big pineapple!
words.card: The pirate carried a *portable* bathtub to every *port*!
